rationale: Sympathetic paragangliomas arise anywhere along the sympathetic chain from the skull base to the pelvis (posterior mediastinum, retroperitoneum, organ of Zuckerkandl, bladder/prostate region), spanning essentially all the connective/soft-tissue (C47) and paraganglia (C75) subsites in the ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.

rationale: Head and neck paragangliomas are, by definition, confined to the head and neck (carotid body, jugulotympanic region, vagal and laryngeal paraganglia); they do not occur across the body-wide sympathetic-chain soft-tissue sites or the heart (C380) included in the code ceiling, so they occupy only the head/neck subset.
source_name: Radiology: Imaging Cancer - Head and Neck Paragangliomas: molecular landscape

rationale: Parasympathetic paragangliomas are found almost exclusively in the head and neck / skull base along the glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves (carotid body, jugulotympanic, vagal, laryngeal), a proper subset of the code ceiling which also spans body-wide sympathetic soft-tissue sites and the heart.

source_name: PubMed 18224469 - Sporadic paraganglioma (parasympathetic tumors found almost exclusively in neck and skull base)

Per WHO 5th ed, central conventional chondrosarcoma is a chondrogenic BONE tumor that is intramedullary in origin, so it is restricted to the skeletal (C40/C41) codes and does not arise in the laryngeal (C32), nasal cavity (C300) or paranasal sinus (C31) sites also present in this code's ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma, summarizing WHO 5th ed

rationale: Grade 1 (conventional) chondrosarcoma NOS is a generic graded cartilaginous malignancy occurring across the code's ceiling, including bone as well as laryngeal and sinonasal cartilage; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma

rationale: Central (intramedullary) low-grade chondrosarcoma is by definition an intraosseous bone tumor, restricted to the skeletal codes and not the laryngeal/nasal/sinus soft-cartilage sites in the ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma, WHO 5th ed

rationale: Peripheral chondrosarcoma arises within the cartilage cap of a pre-existing osteochondroma (a bone-surface lesion), so it is a skeletal tumor restricted to bone (C40/C41), not the laryngeal/nasal/sinus sites in the ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma, WHO 5th ed

rationale: Secondary peripheral chondrosarcoma develops from the cartilage cap of an osteochondroma and is a chondrogenic bone tumor per WHO 5th ed; it is restricted to skeletal sites and does not arise in the larynx/nasal cavity/sinus present in the ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma, WHO 5th ed

rationale: Chondroblastoma occurs throughout the skeleton (long bones, flat bones, pelvis, spine, ribs, hands/feet and craniofacial bones), so within its bone-only ceiling it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Archives of Pathology & Laboratory Medicine - Chondroblastoma: An Update

rationale: EMC arises in deep soft tissue across the body (proximal extremities/limb girdles most common, but also trunk, retroperitoneum, head and neck), spanning its soft-tissue-only ceiling; predilection for the thigh is not a restriction to a proper subset.
source_name: Cancers (2020) Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma: State of the Art

rationale: Synonym of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma; occurs in deep soft tissue at multiple sites across the connective/soft-tissue ceiling, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Cancers (2020) Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma: State of the Art

rationale: Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma has a widespread distribution involving both bone (craniofacial, ribs/chest wall, spine, extremities) and extraskeletal soft tissue (~30-40% of cases), covering both compartments of its bone-plus-soft-tissue ceiling.
source_name: Skeletal Radiology (2020) Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma: imaging and clinical findings

rationale: Clear cell chondrosarcoma has a predilection for the epiphyses of long bones (proximal femur/humerus) but also arises in flat bones, spine, ribs, hands/feet and skull; a predilection within the skeleton is not a restriction to a proper subset of its bone-only ceiling.
source_name: Diagnostic Cytopathology (2020) Clear-cell chondrosarcomas

rationale: Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma arises across the chondrosarcoma spectrum, chiefly in skeletal sites (pelvis, femur, humerus) but also reported in sinonasal/craniofacial sites; evidence does not cleanly restrict it to a proper subset of its ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma

rationale: Giant cell tumor/sarcoma of bone is a skeletal neoplasm (long bones, flat bones, spine, pelvis, and rarely skull/facial bones); it does not arise from the nasal cavity (C300) or paranasal sinus (C31) mucosal sites also present in this code's ceiling, so it is restricted to the bone codes.
source_name: RadioGraphics (2013) Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Review

term: Giant cell tumor of bone, dedifferentiated
normalized_term: Giant cell tumor of bone dedifferentiated
rationale: A bone-based giant cell tumor variant; occurs in the skeleton (predominantly long bones, also axial and craniofacial bones) and not in the nasal cavity/sinus mucosal sites in the ceiling, restricting it to the bone codes.
source_name: RadioGraphics (2013) Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Review

term: Giant cell tumor of bone, malignant
normalized_term: Giant cell tumor of bone malignant
rationale: Malignant giant cell tumor of bone is a skeletal neoplasm arising in long bones, flat/axial bones and rarely craniofacial bones; it does not arise in the nasal cavity or paranasal sinus mucosa in the ceiling, so it is restricted to the bone codes.
source_name: RadioGraphics (2013) Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Review

rationale: Osteoclastoma is a synonym for giant cell tumor of bone, a skeletal tumor; it does not arise from nasal cavity/paranasal sinus mucosa in the ceiling, restricting it to the bone codes.
source_name: RadioGraphics (2013) Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Review

term: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath, malignant
normalized_term: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath malignant
rationale: Malignant tenosynovial giant cell tumor arises from synovium/tendon sheaths in soft tissue across multiple limb and other connective-tissue sites, spanning its soft-tissue-only ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9252/3 Malignant tenosynovial giant cell tumor, C49._)

rationale: This tumor arises from synovial/tendon-sheath soft tissue at multiple anatomic sites (hands, feet, large joints and other soft tissues), covering the connective/soft-tissue ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9252/3, C49._)

rationale: Adamantinoma of long bones occurs in ~97% of cases in the long tubular limb bones (chiefly tibia, also fibula/humerus/radius/femur); it is restricted to limb bones (C40) and effectively excludes the axial/craniofacial bones (C41) present in the ceiling.
source_name: In Vivo (2021) Adamantinoma: An Updated Review

rationale: By definition a tumor of the long (limb) bones; ~97% arise in long tubular bones, predominantly the tibia, restricting it to limb-bone codes (C40) rather than the axial/craniofacial bones (C41) in the ceiling.
source_name: In Vivo (2021) Adamantinoma: An Updated Review

rationale: Classic adamantinoma is a biphasic neoplasm of long bones that predominantly involves the tibia (and occasionally fibula), restricting it to the limb-bone codes (C40) and not the axial/craniofacial bones (C41) in the ceiling.
source_name: Clinical Tree - Adamantinoma of Long Bone (Dorfman/Czerniak)

rationale: Classic adamantinoma is a long-bone tumor predominantly of the tibia/fibula, restricting it to limb-bone codes (C40) rather than the axial and craniofacial bones (C41) present in the ceiling.
source_name: Clinical Tree - Adamantinoma of Long Bone

rationale: A variant of long-bone adamantinoma, which arises almost exclusively in the long (limb) bones, chiefly the tibia; restricted to the limb-bone codes (C40) rather than axial/craniofacial bones (C41) in the ceiling.
source_name: In Vivo (2021) Adamantinoma: An Updated Review

rationale: Tibial adamantinoma by name and clinical reality arises in the tibia (the long bones of the lower limb, C402), which is the overwhelmingly dominant site (80-85% of adamantinomas); this is a strict single-site subset of the code's bone ceiling.
source_name: In Vivo (2021) Adamantinoma: An Updated Review

rationale: An odontogenic sarcoma of the tooth-bearing jaws; its ceiling is already limited to the jaw bones (C410 bones of skull/face incl. maxilla, C411 mandible) and the entity occurs in both jaws, so it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9290/3 odontogenic)

rationale: An odontogenic jaw sarcoma; ceiling already restricted to jaw bones (C410, C411) and the tumor occurs in both maxilla and mandible, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9290/3)

rationale: An odontogenic jaw sarcoma occurring in both the maxilla and mandible; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411), so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9290/3)

rationale: Under 9310/3 this is the jaw (odontogenic) ameloblastoma/adamantinoma; its ceiling is only the jaw-bone codes (C410 skull/face incl. maxilla, C411 mandible) and it occurs in both, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9310/3 Ameloblastoma, malignant)

rationale: Malignant ameloblastoma of the jaws arises in both the mandible (majority) and maxilla; the ceiling is already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411), so it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9310/3)

rationale: Metastasizing ameloblastoma originates in the jaws (mandible more than maxilla); the ceiling is already limited to jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) and both are involved, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9310/3)

rationale: Synonym for metastasizing ameloblastoma of the jaws; occurs in both mandible and maxilla, and the ceiling is already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411), so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9310/3)

rationale: Odontogenic sarcoma of the jaws; ceiling already limited to jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) with occurrence in both, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3 odontogenic)

rationale: Odontogenic jaw sarcoma; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) and the entity occurs in both jaws, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Ameloblastic fibrosarcoma is an odontogenic sarcoma of the jaws arising in both mandible and maxilla; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411), so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Synonym for odontogenic (ameloblastic) sarcoma of the jaws; ceiling limited to jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) and occurs in both jaws, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Odontogenic sarcoma of the tooth-bearing jaws; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) with involvement of both, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Odontogenic sarcoma NOS arises in the jaws; ceiling limited to jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) and both jaws are involved, so it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Plural synonym for odontogenic sarcoma of the jaws; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) with both jaws involved, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

term: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions
normalized_term: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1 nonETS fusions
rationale: This family of undifferentiated round cell sarcomas arises across bone, soft tissue and the central nervous system depending on fusion partner, spanning the multiple compartments in its broad ceiling; a generic multi-site sarcoma descriptor, not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Surgical Pathology Clinics (2025) Sarcomas with EWSR1::non-ETS fusion

normalized_term: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1 FUS::NFATC2
rationale: EWSR1/FUS::NFATC2 sarcoma predominates in the long bones but is also reported in soft tissue (extremities, retroperitoneum, chest wall, head and neck), covering both bone and soft-tissue compartments of the ceiling; a predilection for long bones is not a clean proper-subset restriction.
source_name: Surgical Pathology Clinics (2025) Sarcomas with EWSR1::non-ETS fusion

rationale: EWSR1::PATZ1 sarcoma arises in deep soft tissue (chest/abdominal wall, extremities), head and neck, and the central nervous system; it is a multi-compartment (soft tissue plus CNS) entity rather than being restricted to a single clean proper subset of the broad ceiling.
source_name: Surgical Pathology Clinics (2025) Sarcomas with EWSR1::non-ETS fusion

term: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1::non-ETS fusions
normalized_term: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1::nonETS fusions
rationale: Synonym for the EWSR1-non-ETS round cell sarcoma family, which occurs across bone, soft tissue and CNS depending on fusion partner; a generic multi-site descriptor, not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Surgical Pathology Clinics (2025) Sarcomas with EWSR1::non-ETS fusion

rationale: CIC-rearranged sarcoma predominates in deep soft tissue (~85%) but also occurs in viscera (~10%), bone (<5%) and the central nervous system, spanning multiple compartments of its broad ceiling; a soft-tissue predilection is not a proper-subset restriction.
source_name: Cancers (2022) CIC-Rearranged Sarcomas

rationale: CIC::DUX4 is the canonical CIC fusion; these sarcomas arise predominantly in soft tissue but are also documented in bone and the central nervous system, covering multiple compartments of the ceiling rather than a single proper subset.
source_name: Cancers (2022) CIC-Rearranged Sarcomas

rationale: Reports suggest CIC::NUTM1 has a distinct tropism for the axial skeleton and, in the CNS literature, is the most common CIC fusion partner in intracranial tumors; the site data are conflicting and based on very few cases, so a proper-subset restriction cannot be established with confidence.
source_name: Cancers (2022) CIC-Rearranged Sarcomas
proposed_site_labels: Connective, subcutaneous and other soft tissues, NOS
proposed_site_rationale: [within ceiling / SMVL-valid] CIC-rearranged sarcomas most often arise in soft tissue ('Most tumors have a predilection to occur in the soft tissue (87%)', limb > trunk > head and neck), with rare bone/visceral/CNS primaries; the ultra-rare CIC-NUTM1 variant 'seems to have distinct anatomic tropism for the axial skeleton' (reported CIC-NUTM1 sarcomas affecting the spine). Soft tissue = C49* (C499 NOS) and axial skeleton/vertebral column = C412. Both C499 and C412 are present in the code's ceiling_codes, so in_ceiling.
proposed_site_source_name: Mancarella C et al. CIC-Rearranged Sarcomas: An Intriguing Entity. PMC9657047 (2022)

term: CNS Ewing family tumor with CIC alteration
normalized_term: CNS Ewing family tumor with CIC alteration
rationale: This term denotes CIC-rearranged sarcoma arising primarily in the central nervous system, a distinct entity recognized in the 2021 WHO Classification of CNS Tumors; it is by definition restricted to the CNS/meninges/nerve codes within this code's broad bone/soft-tissue/CNS ceiling.
source_name: Brain Pathology (2024) CIC/ATXN1-rearranged tumors in the CNS; WHO CNS 5th ed

rationale: BCOR-rearranged sarcoma is an undifferentiated round cell sarcoma arising in bone and soft tissue (pelvis, extremities, paraspinal, rarely kidney/lung); it does not arise as a primary CNS/meningeal tumor, so it is restricted to the bone/soft-tissue portion of the ceiling, excluding the meninges/brain/spinal-cord codes (C70-C72).
source_name: Sarcoma Foundation of America (WHO 5th ed. Soft Tissue & Bone)

rationale: BCOR::CCNB3 sarcoma arises predominantly in bone and secondarily in soft tissue (pelvis, lower extremity, paraspinal region); it is not a primary CNS tumor, restricting it to the bone/soft-tissue portion of the ceiling and excluding CNS codes C70-C72.
source_name: Cureus 2025 (PMC12417219), citing WHO 5th ed.

term: Primitive myxoid mesenchymal tumor of infancy
normalized_term: Primitive myxoid mesenchymal tumor of infancy
rationale: Primitive myxoid mesenchymal tumor of infancy arises mainly in the deep somatic soft tissues of the trunk, head/neck, extremities and rarely retroperitoneum; it is a soft-tissue neoplasm and is restricted to the soft-tissue/retroperitoneal portion of the ceiling.
source_name: Sarcoma Foundation of America (WHO 5th ed. Soft Tissue & Bone)

rationale: Infantile undifferentiated round cell sarcoma (BCOR-ITD) arises mainly in the soft tissues of the trunk, retroperitoneum and head/neck, typically sparing bone and CNS; restricted to the soft-tissue/retroperitoneal portion of the ceiling.
source_name: Sarcoma Foundation of America (WHO 5th ed. Soft Tissue & Bone)

rationale: Sarcomas with BCOR genetic alterations arise in bone and soft tissue (and rarely kidney); they are not primary CNS tumors, restricting them to the bone/soft-tissue portion of the ceiling and excluding CNS codes C70-C72.
source_name: Sarcoma Foundation of America (WHO 5th ed. Soft Tissue & Bone)

rationale: Chordoma arises from notochordal remnants restricted to the axial skeleton (skull base/clivus, mobile spine vertebrae, sacrococcyx); it does not arise in limb bones, adrenal (C74) or endocrine glands (C75), so it is restricted to the axial bone subset of the ceiling.
source_name: J Clin Imaging Sci 2022 (PMC9479632) / WHO 5th ed. Soft Tissue & Bone

rationale: Conventional chordoma arises from notochordal remnants of the axial skeleton (skull base, vertebral column, sacrum); restricted to axial bone, excluding limb bones, adrenal and other endocrine sites in the ceiling.
source_name: J Clin Imaging Sci 2022 (PMC9479632) / WHO 5th ed. Soft Tissue & Bone

rationale: Poorly differentiated chordoma is a SMARCB1-deficient axial-skeleton chordoma arising predominantly in the skull base/clivus and cervical spine, occasionally sacrum; restricted to the axial bone subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Am J Surg Pathol / PubMed 29483606 (WHO 5th ed.)

rationale: Chondroid chordoma is a chordoma subtype of the axial skeleton, classically the skull base/clivus; restricted to the axial bone subset of the ceiling, excluding limb bones, adrenal and endocrine sites.
source_name: J Clin Imaging Sci 2022 (PMC9479632) / WHO 5th ed. Soft Tissue & Bone

rationale: Dedifferentiated chordoma is a high-grade axial-skeleton chordoma (skull base, spine, sacrum); restricted to the axial bone subset of the ceiling, excluding limb bones, adrenal and endocrine sites.
source_name: J Clin Imaging Sci 2022 (PMC9479632) / WHO 5th ed. Soft Tissue & Bone

rationale: CNS ganglioneuroblastoma is a central nervous system embryonal/neuronal tumor arising in the brain and spinal cord, distinct from peripheral (sympathetic) ganglioneuroblastoma; restricted to the CNS parenchyma codes of the ceiling.

proposed_site_rationale: [outside ceiling / not SMVL-valid for this code] PFA ependymoma is by definition a posterior-fossa tumor arising in and around the fourth ventricle (cerebellum/brainstem region), tending to involve the roof/lateral aspects of the fourth ventricle with extension into the foramen of Luschka. Note C715 is within the listed ceiling but represents supratentorial 'Ventricle NOS'; the true 4th-ventricle posterior-fossa location is not represented, hence overall outside_ceiling.

normalized_term: Adult T cell leukemia lymphoma HTLV 1 associated

rationale: Synonym for the systemic ATLL entity; disseminated disease not confined to a proper subset of ceiling sites.

normalized_term: Adult T cell lymphoma leukemia acute

normalized_term: Adult T cell lymphoma leukemia chronic

normalized_term: Adult T cell lymphoma leukemia smoldering

source_name: StatPearls, Adult T-Cell Leukemia (NCBI Bookshelf NBK558968)

normalized_term: Chronic adult T cell leukemia lymphoma
rationale: Chronic clinical variant of systemic ATLL; defined by hematologic/organ criteria (skin, lung, liver, lymphocytosis), not anatomically confined to a subset of the ceiling.
source_name: StatPearls, Adult T-Cell Leukemia (NCBI Bookshelf NBK558968)

normalized_term: Cutaneous adult T cell leukemia lymphoma
rationale: Cutaneous-type ATLL is skin-predominant, but skin (C44*) is not within this term's ceiling of bone marrow (C421) and CNS (C728/C729); within the ceiling it is not restricted to a CNS-only or marrow-only subset, so no valid proper subset applies.
source_name: StatPearls, Adult T-Cell Leukemia (NCBI Bookshelf NBK558968)

normalized_term: Lymphomatous adult T cell leukemia lymphoma
rationale: Lymphomatous clinical variant of systemic ATLL; multiorgan lymphomatous presentation, not confined to a proper subset of the bone-marrow+CNS ceiling.

normalized_term: Smoldering adult T cell leukemia lymphoma
rationale: Smoldering clinical variant of systemic ATLL defined by indolent hematologic/organ criteria; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: StatPearls, Adult T-Cell Leukemia (NCBI Bookshelf NBK558968)

SEER training explicitly lists 'reserve cell' as a synonym of small cell carcinoma and notes these are central lesions in the bronchus/hilum of the lung. Lung (C349) and main bronchus (C340) are the sites of origin, both in-ceiling. (The cervical 'reserve cell' usage is a separate archaic descriptor; the ICD-O 8041/3 designation ties the term to bronchial small cell carcinoma.) Note: small cell carcinoma also arises at extrapulmonary sites (cervix, prostate, GI, bladder, head/neck); lung is the canonical/most common primary.

proposed_site_rationale: [within ceiling / SMVL-valid] Monocytoid B-cell lymphoma (nodal marginal zone lymphoma) characteristically involves peripheral lymph nodes, with a documented propensity for paraparotid/intraparotid and head-and-neck nodes; the tumor cells occupy the marginal-zone/sinusoidal-interfollicular compartments of the node. rationale: Extraosseous/extramedullary plasmacytoma is a plasma-cell neoplasm arising in soft tissue outside bone; although ~80% occur in the upper aerodigestive (head/neck) mucosa, authoritative sources document occurrence throughout the body (GI tract, lymph nodes, bladder, breast, thyroid, testis, parotid, skin, CNS), spanning essentially the entire ceiling. The head/neck predilection is a frequency observation, not an anatomic restriction, so the term is not confined to a proper subset.
source_name: NCI SEER Hematopoietic Database (ICD-O-3.2) — Plasmacytoma, extramedullary

Although derived from thymic tissue, the anatomic site of origin/location is the lung (C349). C349 is outside this code's ceiling (ceiling contains only thymus C379 and anterior mediastinum C380). The in-ceiling thymus code C379 does not capture the intrapulmonary location.
proposed_site_source_name: Primary Intrapulmonary Thymoma Appearing as a Solitary Pulmonary Nodule (PMC8548194): 'PITs are defined as tumors of thymic origin with the characteristic histological features of thymoma, situated below the visceral pleura or completely surrounded by lung parenchyma, without a mediastinal component.'

The term is therefore restricted to the adrenal gland, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes mediastinal codes C381-C398).
source_name: Arch Pathol Lab Med (Tischler), summarizing WHO classification

rationale: As with pheochromocytoma NOS, WHO defines pheochromocytoma (including metastatic/malignant) as an intra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma; extra-adrenal/mediastinal tumors are paragangliomas. The named entity is restricted to the adrenal gland, a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Arch Pathol Lab Med (Tischler), summarizing WHO classification

rationale: Pulmonary blastoma (pneumoblastoma) is defined by WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed as a rare subtype of lung cancer (biphasic tumor of the lung); it is a bronchopulmonary parenchymal tumor and is not a tracheal entity. It is thus restricted to lung/bronchus, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes trachea C339 and respiratory NOS C390).
source_name: J Natl Cancer Center 2024 (citing WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed)

rationale: WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed defines pulmonary blastoma as a rare biphasic subtype of lung cancer arising in the lung; it is a bronchopulmonary tumor, not a tracheal one. Restricted to lung/bronchus, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes trachea C339 and respiratory NOS C390).
source_name: J Natl Cancer Center 2024 (citing WHO Thoracic Tumours 5th ed)

rationale: Pleuropulmonary blastoma originates from either the lung or pleura in children. The code's ceiling consists entirely of lung/bronchus subsites (C340-C349); PPB occurs across these lung sites, so no proper-subset restriction exists within the ceiling.
source_name: Iran J Cancer Prevention 2012 (PPB review)

rationale: PPB type I (cystic) arises in the lung/pleura of young children; it shares the same lung anatomic distribution as the parent entity. The ceiling is entirely lung/bronchus subsites, so the type-specific term is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Iran J Cancer Prevention 2012 (PPB review)

rationale: PPB type II (mixed cystic/solid) is a histologic progression variant with the same lung/pleura anatomic distribution as the parent entity. The ceiling is entirely lung/bronchus subsites, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: Iran J Cancer Prevention 2012 (PPB review)

rationale: PPB type III (solid) is a histologic-grade variant with the same lung/pleura distribution as the parent entity. The ceiling is entirely lung/bronchus subsites, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: Iran J Cancer Prevention 2012 (PPB review)

rationale: PPB type Ir (type I regressed) is a histologic variant with the same lung/pleura anatomic distribution as the parent entity. The ceiling is entirely lung/bronchus subsites, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: Iran J Cancer Prevention 2012 (PPB review)

term: Pleuropulmonary blastoma, type Ir (type I regressed)
rationale: PPB type Ir (type I regressed) is a histologic variant with the same lung/pleura anatomic distribution as the parent entity. The ceiling is entirely lung/bronchus subsites, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: Iran J Cancer Prevention 2012 (PPB review)

rationale: Synovial sarcoma (including epithelioid/monophasic patterns) is a translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma that can arise as a primary tumor at all sites in this ceiling (lung, mediastinum, prostate, kidney). The epithelioid-cell descriptor is a morphologic pattern, not an anatomic restriction; no proper-subset limitation is supported.
source_name: WHO Blue Books, Thoracic Tumours 5th ed (structures)

term: Germ cell tumor with associated hematological malignancy
normalized_term: Germ cell tumor with associated hematological malignancy
rationale: This entity is a recognized phenomenon of mediastinal (thymic/mediastinum) germ cell tumors, and the code's ceiling is confined to thymus and mediastinum (C379, C381-C383). The term occurs across essentially the entire mediastinal ceiling, so there is no proper-subset restriction within it.
source_name: WHO Blue Books, Thoracic Tumours 5th ed (structures)

rationale: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis is a diffuse pulmonary neoplastic process; the code's ceiling is composed entirely of lung/bronchus subsites (C340-C349). Because it involves the lung broadly, there is no proper-subset restriction within the ceiling.
source_name: WHO Blue Books, Thoracic Tumours 5th ed (structures)

rationale: Lymphangiomyomatosis is a synonym for lymphangioleiomyomatosis, a diffuse pulmonary process; the ceiling is entirely lung/bronchus subsites (C340-C349), so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: WHO Blue Books, Thoracic Tumours 5th ed (structures)

rationale: Esthesioneuroblastoma arises from the specialized olfactory neuroepithelium of the upper nasal cavity, cribriform plate/ethmoid region, and olfactory nerve; ectopic occurrence in paranasal sinuses other than the ethmoid is vanishingly rare. It is therefore restricted to nasal cavity, ethmoid sinus, and olfactory nerve, a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes maxillary C310, frontal C312, sphenoid C313 sinuses and other cranial nerves).
source_name: Head Neck Pathol 2009 (Thompson, Olfactory Neuroblastoma)

rationale: Olfactory neuroblastoma (a synonym for esthesioneuroblastoma) arises from olfactory neuroepithelium in the upper nasal cavity, cribriform plate/ethmoid, and olfactory nerve; ectopic paranasal-sinus (non-ethmoid) tumors are vanishingly rare. Restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling (excludes maxillary, frontal, sphenoid sinuses and non-olfactory cranial nerves).
source_name: Head Neck Pathol 2009 (Thompson, Olfactory Neuroblastoma)

rationale: Extracavitary PEL presents as solid tumor masses in lymph nodes and extranodal sites including GI tract, skin, lung, and CNS. Within this ceiling it involves lung (C340-C349) and lymph nodes (C770-C779) among others, spreading across ceiling sites rather than being confined to a proper subset.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - PEL/EC-PEL

normalized_term: Fibrin associated diffuse large B cell lymphoma
rationale: Fibrin-associated LBCL is defined by its microenvironment (chronic fibrin deposition) rather than by anatomic site, arising throughout the body at cardiac myxomas/valves, cysts and pseudocysts (spleen, kidney, adrenal, ovary), breast implants, hematomas, and endovascular grafts. As a microenvironment-defined, multi-site entity it is not restricted to a proper anatomic subset.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - FA-LBCL

normalized_term: Fibrin associated large B cell lymphoma
rationale: Fibrin-associated LBCL arises at sites of chronic fibrin deposition throughout the body (cardiac myxomas/valves, cysts/pseudocysts, breast implants, hematomas, endovascular grafts); it is defined by its fibrinous microenvironment, not by anatomic location, so it is not restricted to a proper anatomic subset.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - FA-LBCL

normalized_term: Fluid overload associated large B cell lymphoma
rationale: Fluid overload-associated LBCL presents as serous body-cavity effusions without detectable tumor masses, lymphadenopathy, or organ involvement, occurring in the pleural (majority), pericardial, and peritoneal cavities. Within this ceiling it is confined to pleura (C384) and pericardium (C380); peritoneum is not in the ceiling, and it does not involve the lung parenchyma, mediastinal tissue, bone marrow, spleen, or lymph nodes, so it is restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - FO-LBCL

rationale: A synonym for fluid overload-associated LBCL, which presents as serous effusions confined to body cavities (pleural, pericardial, peritoneal) without tumor masses or organ involvement. Within this ceiling it is confined to pleura (C384) and pericardium (C380), a proper subset (excludes lung parenchyma, mediastinal tissue, bone marrow, spleen, lymph nodes).
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - FO-LBCL

normalized_term: KSHV HHV8 negative effusion based lymphoma
rationale: This is the WHO/ICC synonym for fluid overload-associated LBCL, an HHV8-negative effusion-based large B-cell lymphoma confined to serous body cavities (pleural, pericardial, peritoneal) without masses or organ involvement. Within this ceiling it is confined to pleura (C384) and pericardium (C380), a proper subset.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - FO-LBCL/effusion-based

rationale: Classic PEL presents as body-cavity effusions but disseminates, and extracavitary lesions occur in the lung, lymph nodes, GI tract, skin, and CNS. Because documented PEL involvement within this ceiling includes lung (C340-C349) and lymph nodes (C770-C779) in addition to serous cavities, the umbrella term is not confined to a proper subset.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - PEL

rationale: Primary mediastinal (thymic) large B-cell lymphoma arises from thymic B cells in the anterior mediastinum; SEER codes it to thymus (C379) or mediastinum (C383). The code's ceiling is confined to thymus and mediastinum (C379, C381-C383), which is exactly this entity's home, so there is no proper-subset restriction within the ceiling.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - PMBL

normalized_term: Primary mediastinal large B cell lymphoma
rationale: PMBL arises from thymic B cells and is coded to thymus (C379) or mediastinum (C383) per SEER. The ceiling is confined to thymus and mediastinum (C379, C381-C383), matching the entity's anatomic home, so no proper-subset restriction exists within the ceiling.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - PMBL

rationale: Thymic (primary mediastinal) large B-cell lymphoma is of putative thymic B-cell origin arising in the mediastinum, coded to thymus (C379) or mediastinum (C383). The ceiling is confined to thymus and mediastinum (C379, C381-C383), matching the entity's home, so there is no proper-subset restriction within the ceiling.
source_name: SEER Hematopoietic Project (WHO 5th ed) - PMBL/thymic LBCL

rationale: Without a 'ductal' qualifier, 'cribriform carcinoma in situ' can denote an in-situ cribriform lesion of breast, cutaneous adnexal, or conjunctival/eye origin; published literature does not clearly restrict this exact term to a single organ within the code's skin+breast+eye ceiling.

proposed_site_rationale: [within ceiling / SMVL-valid] "Cribriform carcinoma in situ" corresponds to the well-defined cribriform pattern of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of the breast; cribriform is one of the five recognized DCIS architectural patterns and cribriform-pattern in-situ carcinoma is characteristically a breast lesion arising in the breast ductal-lobular system. StatPearls (NCBI) lists cribriform among the DCIS architectural patterns confined to breast ducts. Breast (C509) is inside the code's ceiling. Cribriform in-situ carcinoma is not a defined distinct primary of skin or eye, so breast is the best-supported single site of origin.
proposed_site_source_name: Breast Ductal Carcinoma in Situ. StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf), 2023 — "The 5 major architectural patterns are comedo, cribriform, micropapillary, papillary, and solid ... confined within the basement membrane" (breast ducts).

proposed_site_rationale: [within ceiling / SMVL-valid] Primary cutaneous acral CD8+ T-cell lymphoma (now lymphoproliferative disorder) has a striking predilection for acral skin, above all the ear, followed by the nose/face, feet and hands. External ear (C442), skin of face/nose (C443), skin of lower limb/foot (C447), and skin of upper limb/hand (C446) are all inside the code's skin ceiling.

source_name: PubMed / Am J Surg Pathol (PMID 23664485) - Tubular adenoma of the urinary tract: a newly described entity
